correctness.rationale: The Poisson parity moments give an exact nonstationary covariance. Because the observed bit takes only two values, its conditional-mean estimator is affine, so the posterior mean-square risk is computed exactly. Differentiation produces S(z)=p/z²-(2-p)+2c²(z-p) with Sʺ(z)>0; its endpoint signs (or a perfect-detector quadratic factorization) prove a unique global interior optimum. Implicit differentiation proves strict reliability ordering. A uniform rare-switching expansion yields the complete κ boundary layer and separates the fixed-imperfect/perfect limits; the fast-switching root balance proves the universal half-horizon limit. Exact symbolic checks and independent Poisson simulations corroborate but are not substituted for the proof. Assumptions and boundary c=0 are explicit.

originality.rationale: Actual semantic record queries, published-paper searches, and inspected primary text were compared by mathematical implication. Bäuerle–Gilitschenski–Hanebeck (2014) study the same integrated two-state telegraph process, but use noisy measurements of its integral to filter hidden states, reversing the observation and estimation targets. Pozdnyakov et al. give occupation laws/likelihoods; Michel studies unknown-rate Fisher-optimal repeated sampling. None of these inspected results proves the global one-bit timing or singular boundary layer. Related Gaussian occupation designs do not imply the Poisson-flip result. The exact boundary layer is not claimed from a mere absence of matching terminology; prior equivalent work remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The target signed occupation average is a natural numerical path integral when an on/off system can transmit just one potentially erroneous bit. The result provides a complete optimal estimator and design for all switching and binary channel noise levels, with strict uniqueness and a sharp singular rare-event scaling. The noncommuting perfect-detector and rare-switching limits, including the explicit κ transition curve, identify a qualitatively important detector-resolution regime. It is not a recomputation of a known numerical table or an arbitrary parameter slice; no paper-sized downstream claim is required.
